messages:
Nora K.: Noticed the empty-state card in the Evaluations tab reads: 'No evals yet. Create one to get started.' Feels flat. Can we make it more actionable?
Sam T.: Agreed. UX research showed people responded better to names of next steps. Maybe: 'Create an evaluation to monitor model quality and catch regressions.'
Ivy L.: Love that. Keep it concise though  maybe shorter: 'Create an evaluation to monitor model quality.'
Ben C.: Also propose primary CTA copy: 'Create evaluation' (not 'New eval'). Clearer for first-time users. Secondary could be 'See examples'.
Nora K.: Accessibility nit: ensure the card uses a heading level and proper focus order when keyboard tabbing.
Sam T.: Tone check: avoid 'regressions' in the primary blurb. Use that in the tooltip/details. Primary should be friendly: 'Measure your model's responses with a quick evaluation.'
Ivy L.: Draft strings: heading = 'No evaluations yet', body = 'Measure your model's responses with a quick evaluation.', primary CTA = 'Create evaluation', secondary = 'View examples'.
TooltipBot: Added suggested copy to the docs: https://redwood.internal/docs/evals-empty-state (added by @Sam T.)
Ben C.: I'll update Figma with those tokens and add a small help icon linking to examples.
Nora K.: Can we include an inline example snippet link so users see what an eval looks like? Quick link 'See a sample test'.
Sam T.: Good call. Secondary actions: 'View examples' (opens modal) and a subtle link 'See a sample test' within the body.
Ivy L.: Also add a11y note: color contrast for the subtle link must meet AA.
Nora K.: Final call: heading 'No evaluations yet', body 'Measure your model's responses with a quick evaluation. See a sample test.', primary 'Create evaluation', secondary 'View examples'. Locking these in unless objections.
Ben C.: No objections. Pushing mock now.
Ivy L.: I'll add the accessibility checklist to the ticket.
Nora K.: Thanks team!
